blocks.h2: What to Do if Sewage Is Backing Up

steps.body: No flushing, showers, dishwasher or laundry. Every gallon adds to the backup.

steps.h3: 2. Keep Everyone Out of the Water
steps.body: Sewage carries bacteria. Keep kids and pets away from the basement.
Don't touch outlets, cords or appliances near the water.
Tell us where it's coming up and whether it's raining.

blocks.h2: Why Sewage Backs Up in Elgin Homes

tiles.body: Common in older neighborhoods, especially with big trees nearby.
Storms fill the sewers fast, and water looks for the lowest opening, often your floor drain.
A collapse or low spot stops the flow and collects debris.
Even newer lines clog when these build up together.

blocks.intro: In July 2017, more than 7 inches of rain fell just south of Elgin over two days, and basements flooded across the area.

items.body: Many homes built before 1940 have gravity floor drains below street level. When the sewer fills, that's where water shows up.
Roots, sags and grease cause backups in 1990s and 2000s homes too, especially once a basement is finished and has a bathroom.
A clean line, a backflow valve and an [overhead sewer system](/elgin/overhead-sewer-systems) each solve part of the problem. We'll tell you which your home needs.

blocks.h2: Sewer Backup Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Why does my basement drain back up when it rains?
items.preview: Your line or the public sewer can't carry the storm water.
items.answer: Either your line is partly blocked and overflows when flow increases, or the public sewer is overloaded and pushing back. A camera inspection tells you which.

items.q: Is a sewer backup covered by insurance?
items.preview: Often only with a specific rider. Check your policy.
items.answer: Many homeowner policies only cover sewer backups with a specific rider or endorsement. Check with your insurance agent, ideally before you need it.

items.q: Should I clean it up myself?
items.preview: Small, contained spills, carefully. Large ones need a cleanup company.
items.answer: A small spill on bare concrete can be cleaned with gloves and disinfectant. Anything that reaches carpet, drywall or furniture should be handled by a professional cleanup company.

items.q: How do I prevent another backup?
items.preview: Keep the line clear and add protection if storms are the trigger.
items.answer: Start with a clear, inspected line and regular [sewer maintenance](/elgin/sewer-maintenance). If storms cause it, a backflow valve or [overhead sewer system](/elgin/overhead-sewer-systems) is the long-term fix.

items.q: Several houses on my street backed up. What does that mean?
items.preview: The public sewer was probably overloaded.
items.answer: When several homes back up in the same storm, the public sewer was probably overloaded. Your own line may still have a problem, so a camera check helps you plan the right protection.

items.q: How much does sewer backup service cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the cause. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what caused the backup and how we reach the line. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
